memory_candidates.content: In orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh, WORK-lettered sections (h), (i), etc. are all top-level statements in one flat script (only usage() and is_live() are functions) — a variable set in an earlier WORK item (e.g. excursions_json in WORK (h)) is directly readable, unmodified, by a later WORK item (e.g. WORK (i)) hundreds of lines later with zero threading/parameter-passing needed. When a dispatch describes two WORK items in the same file as needing to 'consult' each other, check for this flat-script scoping before assuming new plumbing is required.

A regression-test fixture that feeds a modified_files/stage_paths entry which does NOT exist on disk (e.g. a synthetic 'completely/unrelated/excursion.sh' never created in $WORKDIR) cannot distinguish 'dropped by a new file_scope filter' from 'silently dropped by git-commit-scoped.sh's own V2 unmatched-pathspec tolerance' — both land on the same exit code/verdict either way. A fails-before/passes-after regression for an excursion-filtering gate needs the excursion path to be a REAL on-disk (and ideally pre-committed) file, with the new assertion checking actual commit contents (git diff/show --name-only), not just exit code or an advisory log line.

Two sibling tasks independently ruled on the same Containment-vs-Overlap predicate distinction at two different pipeline layers (postflight-cycle-commit vs. in-dispatch phase-commit) and converged on the same vocabulary: 'Containment predicate' (one concrete path vs. one task's declared file_scope) as distinct from the Overlap-family --task/V5 contended-path lease (two-or-more tasks declaring the same path); 'drop-and-warn, never refuse the whole commit' per git-staging-scope.md's under-stage-never-over-stage direction; and 'fail OPEN on a missing/malformed file_scope'. When documenting a new instance of this predicate, reuse this existing terminology rather than re-deriving new wording.
